q.s: The first Harappan site to be excavated in independent India was:
q.x: Ropar (Rupnagar) in Punjab, found in 1950, was the first Harappan site dug after Independence.

q.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is NOT located in present-day India?
q.x: Chanhudaro is in Sindh, Pakistan. Ropar (Punjab), Lothal and Dholavira (Gujarat) are in India.

q.s: A row of seven fire altars on a mud-brick platform has been found at the Harappan site of:
q.x: Kalibangan (Rajasthan) has the row of seven fire altars. Lothal, in Gujarat, also has a fire altar.

q.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is NOT located in Gujarat?
q.x: Kalibangan is in Rajasthan; Lothal, Dholavira and Surkotada are in Gujarat.

q.s: Patanjali, the author of the Mahabhashya, was a contemporary of:
q.x: Patanjali, the grammarian who wrote the Mahabhashya on Panini, lived in the time of Pushyamitra Shunga.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT traditionally counted among the navaratnas of Chandragupta II?
q.x: Patanjali lived in the Shunga period. Kalidasa, Amarasimha (Amarakosha) and Varahamihira are counted among the nine gems.

q.s: The gold coin known as 'Mada' was issued by the:
q.x: The Mada was a gold coin of the Kakatiyas of Warangal.

q.s: Which of the following statements about early coinage in Andhra is correct?
o: The Mada was a copper coin of the Ikshvakus.
Kahapana and nikkha are first mentioned in Sangam texts.
The Ikshvaku ruler Santamula I gave away crores of gold coins.
The Kakatiyas issued no gold coins.
q.x: Santamula I's gifts of gold coins are recorded; kahapana and nikkha first appear clearly in Pali texts, and the Mada was a Kakatiya gold coin.

q.s: The legend of Videgha Madhava in the Satapatha Brahmana refers to the:
o: Eastward spread of settlement into the Gangetic plains
Migration of the Aryans to the Deccan
q.x: Videgha Madhava carrying the sacred fire east across the Sadanira stands for the clearing and settlement of the eastern Gangetic lands.

q.s: The Ramayana of Valmiki contains about:
q.x: The Ramayana has about 24,000 verses. About one lakh verses in 18 books describes the Mahabharata.

q.s: The epic that contains about one lakh verses arranged in 18 books (parvas) is the:
q.x: The Mahabharata, with about one lakh verses in 18 parvas, is the longest Indian epic.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the antaranga (inner) limbs of Patanjali's Ashtanga Yoga?
q.x: The inner limbs are Dharana, Dhyana and Samadhi. Pratyahara is the fifth and last of the five outer (bahiranga) limbs.

q.s: The ancient centre of learning Taxila was located in the Mahajanapada of:
q.x: Taxila was the capital of Gandhara and stood on the Uttarapatha, the northern trade route.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas?
q.x: Kalinga is not in the Anguttara Nikaya list; Vatsa (Kaushambi), Gandhara (Taxila) and Avanti (Ujjayini) are.

q.s: The Mulamadhyamakakarika, the basic text of the Madhyamika school of Buddhism, was written by:
q.x: Acharya Nagarjuna, linked with Nagarjunakonda and Amaravati, founded the Madhyamika (Shunyavada) school.

q.s: Which of the following works was NOT written by Ashvaghosha?
q.x: The Pali Visuddhimagga is by Buddhaghosa. The other three are Ashvaghosha's.

q.s: The Kathavatthu, compiled by Moggaliputta Tissa at the Third Buddhist Council, is a part of the:
q.x: The Kathavatthu belongs to the Abhidhamma Pitaka, the philosophical part of the canon.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the Sutta Pitaka?
q.x: The Patimokkha, with 227 rules for monks, is in the Vinaya Pitaka; the Mahaparinibbana Sutta is in the Digha Nikaya and the Dhammapada in the Khuddaka Nikaya.

q.s: The Barabar caves, which carry the inscriptions of Ashoka, are located in the present-day state of:
q.x: The Barabar caves near Gaya in Bihar were given by Ashoka to the Ajivikas.

q.s: Which of the following rock-cut cave sites is NOT a Buddhist site?
q.x: Sittanavasal in Tamil Nadu is a Jain cave shrine known for its paintings; Nasik also carries Gautami Balashri's inscription.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Jainism and Buddhism is correct?
o: Buddhism follows a stricter ahimsa than Jainism.
Both accept the doctrine of karma and rebirth.
Buddhism believes in an eternal soul (jiva) in all things.
q.x: Both religions accept karma and rebirth. Jainism has the stricter ahimsa and the belief in jiva; the Middle Way is Buddhist.

q.s: The Brahmi script of the Ashokan edicts was first deciphered in 1837 by:
q.x: James Prinsep deciphered Brahmi in 1837, starting with the Delhi-Topra pillar edicts.

q.s: The Telugu script has evolved from the ancient script known as:
q.x: Telugu, like most Indian scripts, descends from Brahmi. Kharosthi was used in the north-west.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three classes of Ashokan inscriptions?
q.x: Ashoka's inscriptions are on rocks, pillars and caves (Barabar); he left no copper-plate inscriptions.

q.s: The Rummindei pillar inscription of Ashoka records the:
o: Reduction of the land tax at Lumbini to one-eighth
q.x: At Rummindei Ashoka freed Lumbini, the Buddha's birthplace, from bali and cut the bhaga to one-eighth.

q.s: Which of the following sites does NOT have an Ashokan pillar inscription?
q.x: Girnar near Junagadh has a Major Rock Edict, not a pillar. Delhi-Topra alone has Pillar Edict VII.

q.s: Which of the following Gupta-period law books (smritis) survives complete?
q.x: The Narada smriti survives in full; the Brihaspati and Katyayana smritis survive only in fragments.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Gupta-period law books is correct?
o: The Narada smriti survives only in fragments.
They clearly separated civil and criminal law.
Theft and adultery were treated as civil cases.
q.x: Gupta law books separated civil and criminal law; theft and adultery were criminal. The Narada smriti survives complete; Katyayana's only in fragments.

q.s: Historians who argue for the rise of Indian feudalism around the seventh century cite as evidence the:
o: Decline of long-distance trade, towns and gold coinage
q.x: The feudalism thesis rests on the decline of trade, urban centres and gold coinage, with growing land grants.

q.s: The Gupta-period Dashavatara temple at Deogarh is dedicated to:
q.x: The Deogarh temple, a Panchayatana with a low shikhara, is a Vishnu temple showing the god's ten avataras.

q.s: Which of the following temples does NOT belong to the Gupta period?
q.x: The Kailasa temple at Ellora is a Rashtrakuta monument (8th century). The other three are Gupta temples.

q.s: The Ajanta caves, lost for centuries, were rediscovered in 1819 by the British officer:
q.x: John Smith came upon Ajanta in 1819 while on a tiger hunt. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.

q.s: Aryabhata composed his astronomical work, the Aryabhatiya, in:
q.x: The Aryabhatiya was written in 499 CE; it gives pi as 3.1416. Brahmagupta's work dates to 628 CE.

q.s: Which of the following statements about science in the Gupta age is correct?
o: Aryabhata gave the value of pi as 3.1416.
Bhaskara I wrote a commentary on the Brahmasphutasiddhanta.
The Gwalior inscription of 876 CE shows zero as a dot.
The Aryabhatiya was written in 628 CE.
q.x: Aryabhata gave pi as 3.1416 in the Aryabhatiya (499 CE). Bhaskara I commented on the Aryabhatiya, and the Gwalior inscription shows zero as a small circle.

q.s: The capital of Qutbuddin Aibak, the founder of the Slave dynasty, was:
q.x: Aibak ruled from Lahore and was buried there; Iltutmish made Delhi the capital.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Qutbuddin Aibak is correct?
o: He was bought as a slave by Iltutmish.
He held the office of Amir-i-Akhur under Muhammad Ghori.
He was buried at Mehrauli near the Qutb Minar.
q.x: Aibak was Master of the Stables. It was Aibak who bought Iltutmish; Aibak ruled from Lahore and was buried there.

q.s: The Delhi Sultan who received a letter of investiture from the Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad in 1229 was:
q.x: Iltutmish received caliphal investiture in 1229, which legitimised his rule.

q.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Sultanate kingship is NOT correctly matched?
o: Iltutmish - Investiture from the Abbasid Caliph
Mubarak Shah Khalji - Proclaimed himself Caliph
Alauddin Khalji - Investiture from the Caliph in 1229
q.x: The 1229 investiture was received by Iltutmish; Alauddin put state interest above the ulema.

q.s: The Delhi Sultan who made iqtas hereditary was:
q.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq made iqtas and offices hereditary to win the nobles' goodwill.

q.s: The city of Agra was founded in 1504 by:
q.x: Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in 1504 and made it his capital.

q.s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq obtained about 1,300 Sanskrit manuscripts from the Jawalamukhi temple at:
q.x: Firoz took the manuscripts from Jawalamukhi at Nagarkot (Kangra) and had some translated into Persian.

q.s: The Delhi Sultan who imposed jizya even on Brahmins, who had earlier been exempt, was:
q.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq extended jizya to Brahmins. Women, children and the old remained exempt.

q.s: Under the Delhi Sultans, which of the following was NOT generally exempt from jizya?
q.x: Jizya fell on adult non-Muslim men; women, children and the old were exempt. Sikandar Lodi also imposed it.

q.s: Muhammad bin Tughlaq sent the Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta as his envoy to:
q.x: In 1342 Muhammad bin Tughlaq sent Ibn Battuta as envoy to the Mongol court of China.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Ibn Battuta is correct?
o: He wrote his Rihla in Persian.
Muhammad bin Tughlaq sent him as envoy to Persia.
He served as Qazi of Delhi.
He visited the court of Akbar.
q.x: Ibn Battuta was Qazi of Delhi and was sent as envoy to China; his Rihla is in Arabic.

q.s: Akbar, the son of Humayun and Hamida Banu Begum, was born in 1542 at:
q.x: Akbar was born at Amarkot in Sindh during Humayun's exile; he was crowned at Kalanaur in 1556.

q.s: Humayun recovered Kandahar and Kabul with the help of the Persian ruler:
q.x: Shah Tahmasp of the Safavid dynasty helped Humayun; Shah Abbas I ruled later.

q.s: The Dasbodh was written by Shivaji's traditionally named guru:
q.x: Samarth Ramdas wrote the Dasbodh. Tukaram was Shivaji's contemporary; Eknath lived earlier.

q.s: Shivaji's tutor and the keeper of the Pune jagir was:
q.x: Dadaji Kondadev managed the Pune jagir of Shahji and trained the young Shivaji. Moropant Pingle was later Peshwa.

q.s: The Treaty of Purandar (1665) was signed between Shivaji and the Mughal general:
q.x: Raja Jai Singh of Amber forced Shivaji into the Treaty of Purandar in 1665.

q.s: Shivaji killed the Bijapur general Afzal Khan at Pratapgarh in the year:
q.x: Afzal Khan was killed in 1659; the raid on Shaista Khan was in 1663 and the escape from Agra in 1666.

q.s: The Subsidiary Alliance was accepted by the Peshwa through the Treaty of Bassein (1802) by:
q.x: Peshwa Baji Rao II signed the Treaty of Bassein in 1802, which led to the Second Anglo-Maratha War.

q.s: Which of the following treaties was NOT signed during the Second Anglo-Maratha War?
q.x: The Treaty of Salbai (1782) ended the First Anglo-Maratha War. Deogaon and Surji-Anjangaon (1803) and Rajpurghat (1805) belong to the Second.

q.s: Constantinople, whose fall disturbed the old trade routes to Asia, was captured by the Ottoman Turks in:
q.x: Mehmed II took Constantinople in 1453, pushing Europeans to find a sea route to India.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Age of Discovery is correct?
o: Before the sea route, Venice and Genoa distributed Asian goods in Europe.
The caravel was an instrument for measuring latitude.
Constantinople fell to the Ottomans in 1492.
Prince Henry the Navigator was a Spanish prince.
q.x: Venice and Genoa controlled the distribution of Asian goods. The caravel was a ship, Constantinople fell in 1453, and Prince Henry was Portuguese.

q.s: The first French factory in India was established in 1668 at:
q.x: François Caron set up the first French factory at Surat in 1668; Masulipatnam followed in 1669.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a French settlement in India?
q.x: Tranquebar was a Danish settlement. Yanam, in the Godavari delta, Mahe and Karaikal were French.

q.s: The Portuguese headquarters in India was shifted from Cochin to Goa in 1530 under the governor:
q.x: Nino (Nuno) da Cunha moved the headquarters to Goa in 1530. Albuquerque had captured Goa in 1510.

q.s: Which of the following places was NOT captured by Afonso de Albuquerque?
q.x: Albuquerque took Goa (1510), Malacca (1511) and Hormuz (1515); Diu came under the Portuguese only in 1535.

q.s: In 1800 the Nizam ceded to the East India Company, to pay for the subsidiary force, the region later called the 'Ceded Districts', which is:
q.x: The Nizam ceded the districts of Rayalaseema (Bellary, Cuddapah, Kurnool, Anantapur) in 1800.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT among the 'Ceded Districts' given up by the Nizam in 1800?
q.x: Guntur was part of the Northern Circars. The Ceded Districts formed today's Rayalaseema and Bellary.

q.s: The government-commissioned centenary history of the Revolt of 1857, 'Eighteen Fifty-Seven', was written by:
q.x: S. N. Sen wrote the official centenary volume in 1957.

q.s: The historian who called the Revolt of 1857 'neither First, nor National, nor a War of Independence' was:
q.x: This verdict is R. C. Majumdar's. Savarkar called it the First War of Indian Independence.

q.s: The decisive battle of the Third Carnatic War, in which the English defeated the French in 1760, was the Battle of:
q.x: Eyre Coote defeated the French under Lally at Wandiwash in 1760; Pondicherry fell in 1761.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Anglo-French rivalry in India is correct?
o: The French Company was a private body free of state control.
The English Company was directly run by the Crown.
Bengal's resources after Plassey financed the English wars in the south.
Pondicherry fell to the English before the Battle of Plassey.
q.x: Bengal's revenue after Plassey (1757) paid for the Carnatic campaign. The English Company was private and the French state-controlled; Pondicherry fell in 1761.

q.s: Under the subordinate alliances of 1818, Rajputana states such as Udaipur, Jaipur and Jodhpur gave up control over their:
q.x: They surrendered their external relations for British protection but kept their internal administration.

q.s: The Archaeological Survey of India functions as an attached office of the Ministry of:
q.x: The ASI is under the Ministry of Culture; its motto is 'Pratnakirti Apavarini'.

q.s: Under the AMASR Act, 1958, an 'ancient monument' is one that has been in existence for not less than:
q.x: The Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958 covers monuments at least 100 years old.

q.s: The University of Madras, which came after the Central Collegiate Institute and the Noble School, was established in:
q.x: Madras University was founded in 1857, along with Calcutta and Bombay, following Wood's Despatch (1854).

q.s: The Marathi newspaper Kesari was founded in 1881 by:
q.x: Tilak founded Kesari (Marathi) and Mahratta (English) in 1881.

q.s: The English newspaper 'The Bengalee', founded by Girish Chandra Ghosh in 1862, was run from 1879 by:
q.x: Surendranath Banerjea ran The Bengalee from 1879. Sisir Kumar Ghosh ran the Amrita Bazar Patrika.

q.s: Thomas Munro, Governor of Madras from 1820 to 1827, is associated with the introduction of the:
q.x: Munro introduced the Ryotwari settlement in Madras, under which the ryot paid revenue directly to the state.

q.s: The Resolution of 1882, called the 'Magna Carta' of local self-government in India, was issued by:
q.x: Lord Ripon's Resolution of 1882 is the Magna Carta of local self-government. Lord Mayo's 1870 Resolution began financial decentralisation.

q.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1919, local self-government was placed in the category of:
q.x: Under dyarchy, local self-government was a transferred subject under Indian ministers.

q.s: The first Indian to be appointed to the Viceroy's Executive Council, as Law Member in 1909, was:
q.x: Satyendra Prasanna Sinha became Law Member in 1909. K. G. Gupta and Bilgrami were put on the Secretary of State's Council in 1907.

q.s: The Secretary of State for India at the time of the Indian Councils Act, 1909 was:
q.x: The 1909 reforms are named after John Morley (Secretary of State) and Lord Minto (Viceroy).

q.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, the Federal Court was set up at Delhi in the year:
q.x: The Federal Court began functioning at Delhi in October 1937.

q.s: With reference to the Government of India Act, 1935, which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Federal Court was set up at Delhi in 1935.
The All-India Federation came into being in 1937.
The Act provided for provincial autonomy.
It abolished the office of the Secretary of State.
q.x: Provincial autonomy came into force in 1937. The Federal Court began in 1937, the federation never came into being, and the Secretary of State remained.

q.s: B. R. Ambedkar's 'Annihilation of Caste', which rebuked Gandhi's approach to caste, was published in:
q.x: Annihilation of Caste appeared in 1936. 1927 was the Mahad Satyagraha, 1932 the Poona Pact.

q.s: B. R. Ambedkar was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in:
q.x: Ambedkar received the Bharat Ratna in 1990. He died in 1956.

q.s: Kandukuri Veeresalingam opened his girls' school at Innispeta in 1881 in the town of:
q.x: Veeresalingam's work was centred at Rajahmundry, where he also set up the widow home Vitantu Saranalayam.

q.s: The first Telugu to become Vice-Chancellor of Madras University was:
q.x: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu, a Brahmo leader and principal of Pithapuram Raja's College, Kakinada, was knighted in 1924. C. R. Reddy was the first VC of Andhra University.

q.s: Under the Poona Pact (1932), the number of seats reserved for the depressed classes in the provincial legislatures was:
q.x: The Poona Pact gave 148 provincial seats (against 71 in the Communal Award) and 18% of the Central Legislature.

q.s: Gandhi began his fast against the separate electorate for the depressed classes on 20 September 1932 at:
q.x: Gandhi fasted at Yerwada Jail, Poona; the fast ended with the Poona Pact.

q.s: The Lucknow session of the Congress (1916), at which the Moderates and Extremists reunited, was presided over by:
q.x: Ambica Charan Mazumdar presided at Lucknow (1916). Basu presided at Madras (1914).

q.s: The Surat session of 1907, which saw the split between Moderates and Extremists, was presided over by:
q.x: Rash Behari Ghosh presided over the Surat session, which broke up in confusion.

q.s: The book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India', which set out the drain theory, was written by:
q.x: Dadabhai Naoroji wrote it (1901). R. C. Dutt wrote the Economic History of India.

q.s: Which of the following book and author pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: A Nation in the Making - S. N. Banerjea
The Indian Struggle - Subhas Chandra Bose
The Man Who Divided India - Rafiq Zakaria
Poverty and Un-British Rule in India - R. C. Dutt
q.x: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India is by Dadabhai Naoroji.

q.s: The partition of Bengal ordered by Lord Curzon came into effect on:
q.x: Partition took effect on 16 October 1905, observed as a day of mourning; Dacca became capital of Eastern Bengal and Assam.

q.s: The partition of Bengal was annulled at the Delhi Durbar of 1911, when the Viceroy was:
q.x: The annulment was announced in 1911 during Lord Hardinge II's viceroyalty.

q.s: A. M. T. Jackson, the Collector of Nasik, was assassinated in 1909 by:
q.x: Anant Kanhere shot Jackson in 1909. The Chapekar brothers killed Rand in 1897.

q.s: The revolutionary society Abhinav Bharat, modelled on Mazzini's Young Italy, was founded in 1904 by:
q.x: V. D. Savarkar merged his Mitra Mela into Abhinav Bharat in 1904; he was later sentenced to the Andamans.

q.s: The Champaran Agrarian Act of 1918, which followed Gandhi's satyagraha, abolished the system of:
q.x: Tinkathia forced peasants to grow indigo on 3/20 of their land; the 1918 Act abolished it.

q.s: Which of the following struggles was NOT led by Gandhi during 1917-18?
q.x: The Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) was led by Vallabhbhai Patel. The other three were Gandhi's early struggles.

q.s: Gandhi's Champaran, Ahmedabad and Kheda struggles took place during the viceroyalty of:
q.x: All three (1917-18) fell under Lord Chelmsford (1916-21).

q.s: The Non-Cooperation programme was adopted at the special session of the Congress held in September 1920 at:
q.x: The Calcutta special session (September 1920) adopted it; the Nagpur session (December 1920) confirmed it.

q.s: The first phase of the Civil Disobedience Movement came to an end with the:
q.x: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact (March 1931) ended the first phase; the second phase (1932-34) was crushed and withdrawn in 1934.

q.s: The Karachi session of the Congress (March 1931), held soon after the execution of Bhagat Singh, was presided over by:
q.x: Sardar Patel presided over the Karachi session of 29-31 March 1931.

q.s: The resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme adopted at the Karachi session was drafted by:
q.x: Jawaharlal Nehru drafted it, with help from M. N. Roy.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Rash Behari Bose is correct?
o: He fled to Japan after the Hardinge bomb case.
He was tried in the Red Fort INA trials.
He died in independent India in 1950.
q.x: He escaped to Japan in 1915, later headed the Indian Independence League and died in January 1945; he was never tried at the Red Fort.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) is correct?
o: Both the Congress and the League saw grouping of provinces the same way.
The Congress regarded grouping as compulsory.
The League regarded grouping as optional.
The Congress regarded grouping as optional, the League as compulsory.
q.x: For the Congress grouping was optional; for the League it was compulsory, a step towards Pakistan.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Cabinet Mission of 1946?
q.x: The Mission had three Cabinet Ministers: Pethick-Lawrence, Cripps and A. V. Alexander. Wavell was Viceroy.

q.s: The Congress leader who became Premier of the Madras Presidency on 30 April 1946 was:
q.x: Tanguturi Prakasam headed the Madras ministry in 1946. Rajagopalachari had been Premier in 1937.

q.s: Under the Mountbatten Plan, the date of the transfer of power was advanced from June 1948 to:
q.x: The plan of 3 June 1947 brought the transfer forward to 15 August 1947.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Mountbatten Plan is correct?
o: Power was to be transferred under the Government of India Act, 1919.
A common Governor-General for both dominions was permitted.
The transfer date was postponed to June 1948.
A Boundary Commission was set up only for Punjab.
q.x: A common Governor-General was allowed. The 1935 Act was the interim constitution, the date was advanced to 15 August 1947, and both Punjab and Bengal had Boundary Commissions.

q.s: The booklet 'A National Flag for India' (1916) was written by:
q.x: Pingali Venkayya of Machilipatnam, designer of the national flag, published it in 1916.

q.s: Which of the following books was NOT written by B. R. Ambedkar?
q.x: India Divided was written by Rajendra Prasad. The other three are Ambedkar's.

q.s: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956, the number of industries listed in Schedule A, reserved for the State, was:
q.x: Schedule A had 17 industries; Schedule B 12 industries for growing State participation; Schedule C was left to private enterprise.

q.s: The Dubagunta anti-arrack movement of 1992 in Andhra Pradesh began in the district of:
q.x: It began at Dubagunta village in Nellore district and spread across the state.

q.s: The Madras Devadasi (Prevention of Dedication) Act of 1947 was the result of the efforts of:
q.x: Dr Muthulakshmi Reddy led the campaign against the dedication of devadasis.

q.s: After Rajasthan, the second State in India to introduce Panchayati Raj, on 1 November 1959, was:
q.x: Rajasthan began on 2 October 1959 (Nagaur) and Andhra Pradesh followed on 1 November 1959.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, Mandal Praja Parishads replaced Panchayat Samitis by an Act of:
q.x: The 1986 Act set up Mandal Praja Parishads in place of Panchayat Samitis.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the States Reorganisation Commission constituted in 1953?
q.x: The SRC comprised Fazal Ali (chairman), H. N. Kunzru and K. M. Panikkar. B. Gopala Reddy signed the Gentlemen's Agreement for Andhra.

q.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956 provided for a cabinet ratio between Andhra and Telangana of:
q.x: The cabinet was to be shared 60:40 between Andhra and Telangana.

q.s: Hyderabad State was integrated with the Indian Union through Operation Polo on:
q.x: The Nizam surrendered on 17 September 1948 after the police action called Operation Polo.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Hyderabad State before 1956 is correct?
o: The Andhra Jana Sangham grew into the Hyderabad State Congress.
The Andhra Jana Sangham (1921) grew into the Nizam Andhra Mahasabha.
Ramananda Tirtha launched the Join Indian Union movement on 15 August 1947.
q.x: The Andhra Jana Sangham became the Nizam Andhra Mahasabha (first session at Jogipet, 1930). Ramananda Tirtha's movement began on 7 August 1947; Hyderabad joined after Operation Polo.

q.s: The earliest literary reference to the Andhras is found in the:
q.x: The Aitareya Brahmana, in the Sunahshepa story, first names the Andhras; the Rigveda does not mention them.

q.s: In the Sunahshepa story of the Aitareya Brahmana, the Andhras are described as the cursed sons of the sage:
q.x: Vishwamitra cursed fifty of his sons to become Andhras, Pundras, Pulindas and others.

q.s: The Ghatikasthanas of the Vishnukundin period were:
q.x: Ghatikas were centres of Vedic learning; agraharas were land grants to Vedic Brahmins.

q.s: The Ikshvaku king in whose reign the Sriparvata University at Nagarjunakonda is said to have been set up was:
q.x: Tradition links the Sriparvata University to Virapurushadatta, a great patron of Buddhism at Nagarjunakonda.

q.s: Which structure at Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda), the Ikshvaku capital, is thought to have been built with Roman help?
q.x: The Kreeda Vedi, an amphitheatre or sports arena, is thought to show Roman influence. Kummakundam are water tanks.

q.s: The Sarvadeva inscription of the Ikshvaku period, issued by Elisri, is written in:
q.x: Elisri's Sarvadeva inscription is in Sanskrit, while the Gummadidurru record of Ehuvala Santamula is in Prakrit.

q.s: Among the Badami Chalukya rulers, the issue of the first gold coins of South India is credited to:
q.x: Pulakesin II, the greatest Badami Chalukya, is credited with the first South Indian gold coins.

q.s: The founder of the Eastern Chalukya dynasty of Vengi, a brother of Pulakesin II, was:
q.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana, brother of Pulakesin II of Badami, founded Eastern Chalukya rule at Vengi.

q.s: Under the Eastern Chalukyas, the village watchman who had to make good the value of stolen goods if the thief was not caught was the:
q.x: The Talari was the village watchman. The Pradvivaka was the king's adviser on justice.

q.s: The ruler who sent an embassy of 72 merchants to China was:
q.x: Kulottunga I (Chola-Chalukya) sent 72 merchants to China. Saktivarma I's gold coins were found in Arakan.

q.s: The Addanki inscription, the first poetic inscription in Telugu, is composed in the metre:
q.x: Addanki (Pandaranga) is in Taruvoja; the Bezawada inscription of Yuddhamalla II has the first Madhyakkara.

q.s: Telugu, along with Kannada, was declared a classical language of India in the year:
q.x: Telugu and Kannada were declared classical on 31 October 2008. Tamil was first (2004), Sanskrit 2005, Malayalam 2013.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT among the languages given classical status on 3 October 2024?
q.x: Odia was declared classical in 2014. Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali were added in 2024, taking the total to 11.

q.s: The Telugu version of the 'Dasakumara Charita' was written by:
q.x: Mula Ghatika Ketana wrote it and dedicated it to Tikkana.

q.s: Which of the following poets was NOT one of the Kavitrayam who rendered the Mahabharata into Telugu?
q.x: The Kavitrayam are Nannaya, Tikkana and Errana. Ketana wrote the Telugu Dasakumara Charita.

q.s: Warangal finally fell to the Delhi Sultanate in 1323 to the army led by:
q.x: Ulugh Khan (later Muhammad bin Tughlaq) captured Warangal in 1323, ending Kakatiya rule.

q.s: Which of the following commanders did NOT lead an invasion of Warangal in the Kakatiya period?
q.x: Malik Ambar was the Ahmadnagar minister of the 17th century. Kafur (1309-10), Khusrau Khan (1318) and Ulugh Khan (1323) invaded Warangal.

q.s: Which of the following crops was NOT grown in Andhra during the Kakatiya period?
q.x: Maize came to India later from the Americas. Rice, including a fragrant variety near Orugallu, was a major crop.

q.s: During the Kakatiya period, Nirmal was famous for the manufacture of:
q.x: Nirmal was known for knives and sword blades; Warangal was famous for ratna kambalu and carpets.

q.s: The Musunuri chief Kapaya Nayaka helped Hasan Gangu to found the:
q.x: Kapaya Nayaka aided Hasan Gangu against Delhi; later Golconda passed to the Bahmanis by the truce of 1364-65.

q.s: The first capital of the Vijayanagara rulers Harihara I and Bukka I was:
q.x: Anegondi was the first capital; the new city of Vijayanagara ('City of Victory') was completed c. 1343 under Bukka I.

q.s: The royal emblem of the Vijayanagara empire was the:
q.x: The Varaha (boar), associated with Vishnu, was the Vijayanagara royal emblem.

q.s: The Palnadu Haihayas, who claimed descent from Kartavirya Arjuna, ruled from:
q.x: The Palnadu Haihayas ruled from Gurajala; the Kota kings ruled Kammanadu from Dhanyakatakam.

q.s: Brahmanaidu, the minister of Palnadu, opened to all castes, including Dalits, the Chennakesava temple at:
q.x: Brahmanaidu opened the Macherla Chennakesava temple to all and promoted common dining (Chapa Koodu).

q.s: The family history of the Recherla Velamas of Rachakonda is recorded in the:
q.x: The Velugoti Varivamsavali is the Velama family chronicle.

q.s: The Recherla Velama rulers of Rachakonda and Devarakonda were also known as:
q.x: The Recherla Velamas were called Padmanayakas; the Musunuri Nayakas were a separate house.

q.s: The Velama forts of Rachakonda and Devarakonda were finally annexed by:
q.x: Sultan Quli Qutb Shah, founder of the Golconda kingdom, annexed both forts.

q.s: The Sanskrit work on dramaturgy and poetics 'Rasarnava Sudhakara' was written by the Recherla ruler:
q.x: Singabhupala of Rachakonda wrote Rasarnava Sudhakara and the play Ratna Panchalika.

q.s: The Telugu work 'Simhasana Dwatrimsika', telling the 32 throne stories of Vikramaditya, was written by:
q.x: Koravi Goparaju, a poet of the Recherla court, wrote Simhasana Dwatrimsika.

q.s: The Vitthala temple at Hampi, in whose complex the famous stone chariot stands, is also known as the:
q.x: The Vitthala temple is called the Saptaswara Devalayam for its 56 musical pillars; the Hazara Rama temple is separate.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Vitthala temple at Hampi is correct?
o: It is popularly known as the Hazara Rama temple.
Its Ranga mandapa has 108 musical pillars.
The stone chariot stands in its complex.
It was completed under Harihara I.
q.x: The stone chariot is in the Vitthala complex. The temple has 56 musical pillars, was begun under Devaraya II and enlarged by Krishnadevaraya and Achyutaraya; the Hazara Rama is a separate temple.

q.s: In the trade of coastal Andhra, Pedaganjam and Chinaganjam were known for the export of:
q.x: Pedaganjam and Chinaganjam exported salt; Narasapuram cheap calico; Nagulavancha and Nalgonda indigo.

q.s: During the Revolt of 1857 in the Deccan, Raja Venkatappa Nayaka rose against the British at:
q.x: Venkatappa Nayaka of Shorapur rose in 1858; Salar Jung I, the Nizam's Diwan, stayed loyal to the British.

q.s: 'Asamardhuni Jeevayatra', regarded as the first psychological novel in Telugu, was written by:
q.x: Tripuraneni Gopichand wrote Asamardhuni Jeevayatra. Chilakamarti wrote Ramachandra Vijayam.

q.s: 'Kavitva Vicharamu' (1914), a landmark of Telugu literary criticism, was written by:
q.x: C. R. Reddy wrote Kavitva Vicharamu (1914); he later became the first VC of Andhra University.

q.s: P. Anandacharlu, an Andhra leader, presided over the session of the Indian National Congress held in 1891 at:
q.x: P. Anandacharlu presided at Nagpur (1891), the seventh session; he was also secretary of the Madras Mahajana Sabha.

q.s: Nyapathi Subbarao, one of the Andhra delegates at the first session of the INC (1885), came from:
q.x: Nyapathi Subbarao was from Rajahmundry; Gutti Kesava Pillai came from Gooty.

q.s: During Bipin Chandra Pal's tour of Andhra in 1907, his Rajahmundry speech was translated into Telugu by:
q.x: Chilakamarti translated the speech; Pal stayed at Madella Sourayya's house in Rajahmundry.

q.s: 'Mutyala Saralu', which introduced a new metre in modern Telugu poetry, was written by:
q.x: Gurajada Apparao wrote Mutyala Saralu. Andhravali is Rayaprolu's.

q.s: Which of the following works was NOT written by Gurram Jashuva?
q.x: Mutyala Saralu is by Gurajada Apparao. Gabbilam, Firadausi and Kandiseekudu ('The Refugee') are Jashuva's.

q.s: On the division of Bellary district in 1953, the Bellary taluk itself was given to:
q.x: On Justice L. S. Mishra's report, Bellary taluk went to Mysore; Alur and Adoni went to Kurnool and Rayadurg to Anantapur.

q.s: The first editor of the Telugu daily Andhra Prabha (1938) was:
q.x: Khasa Subba Rao was its first editor; Narla Venkateswara Rao edited it later.

q.s: During the Library Movement in Andhra, free copies of books were sent to village libraries by the publishers:
q.x: Vavilala Ramaswamy Sastrulu & Sons supplied the Ramamohan Library and village libraries; the Andhra Granthamala gave similar help.

q.s: The Sangeet Natak Akademi, the national academy of music, dance and drama, was inaugurated on 28 January 1953 by:
q.x: President Rajendra Prasad inaugurated it; the Sahitya Akademi was inaugurated on 12 March 1954.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a national akademi of the Government of India?
q.x: The Telugu Akademi is a State body. The other three are national academies set up in 1953-54.

q.s: The Telugu literary monthly 'Bharati' (1924) was started by:
q.x: Kasinadhuni Nageswara Rao started both Andhra Patrika and Bharati.

q.s: The first communist journal in Telugu was:
q.x: Prajasakti was the first communist Telugu journal.

q.s: Gurram Jashuva's 'Gabbilam' (1941) is modelled on Kalidasa's:
q.x: As in the Meghaduta, a messenger (here a bat) carries a message; Jashuva's bat carries a hungry Dalit's plea to Lord Shiva at Kashi.

q.s: Assaka (Ashmaka), the only Mahajanapada south of the Vindhyas, was located on the banks of the river:
q.x: Assaka lay on the Godavari; the Suttanipata places sage Bavari's ashram there.

q.s: Potana, the capital of Assaka, is identified with Bodhan in the present district of:
q.x: Bodhan is in Nizamabad district (Telangana).

q.s: Muhammad Ghori ended the Ghaznavid dynasty by taking Lahore in the year:
q.x: Ghori ended Ghaznavid rule in 1186; 1192 was the Second Battle of Tarain.

q.s: The Somnath Swabhiman Parv held in January 2026 marked 1,000 years since the attack on the Somnath temple by:
q.x: Mahmud of Ghazni attacked Somnath in 1025-26; the 2026 Parv marked the millennium.

q.s: In sociology, the persistent failure of a family to perform its functions, as through abuse or alcoholism, is called:
q.x: Such persistent failure is termed family dysfunction, not role conflict.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the functions of the family is correct?
o: The family protects only its earning members.
Inheritance means the collective consumption of goods by the family.
Persistent failure of family functions is called role conflict.
By providing socially approved sexual relations, the family prevents social disorder.
q.x: Regulating sexual relations is a core family function. The family protects all members; inheritance is the passing of property and status; persistent failure is dysfunction.

q.s: The sociologist who analysed the concepts of sapinda and gotra in her study of Indian kinship was:
q.x: Irawati Karve wrote 'Kinship Organisation in India'.

q.s: According to G. S. Ghurye, the defining feature of caste is:
q.x: Ghurye held endogamy to be the essence of caste.

q.s: Which of the following statements about marriage laws in India is correct?
o: Registration is optional under the Special Marriage Act, 1954.
Divorce under the Special Marriage Act is provided by Section 13.
Divorce by mutual consent was added to the Indian Divorce Act, 1869 in 2001.
The Anand Marriage Act, 1909 governs Parsi marriages.
q.x: The 2001 amendment added mutual-consent divorce for Christians. Registration is compulsory under the SMA, its divorce section is 27, and the Anand Marriage Act is for Sikhs.

q.s: Untouchability is abolished and its practice forbidden by which Article of the Indian Constitution?
q.x: Article 17 abolishes untouchability; the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 enforces it.

q.s: The book 'Modernization of Indian Tradition' (1973) was written by:
q.x: Yogendra Singh wrote it. Milton Singer studied tradition and modernity in Madras.

q.s: 'Gulamgiri' (1873), a critique of caste slavery, was written by:
q.x: Jyotirao Phule wrote Gulamgiri and founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (1873).

q.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar?
q.x: Gulamgiri is by Jyotirao Phule. Vidyasagar was linked with the Bethune School, the Widow Remarriage Act and Som Prakash.

q.s: ILO Convention No. 182, which India ratified in 2017, deals with the:
q.x: Convention 182 covers the worst forms of child labour; Convention 138 sets the minimum age.

q.s: The World Day Against Child Labour is observed every year on:
q.x: It is observed on 12 June. 20 November is World Children's Day.

q.s: A common feature of recent youth protests such as those in Bangladesh (2024) and Nepal (Gen Z, 2025) was:
o: Leadership by a formal central committee
Control by a single political party
Leaderless organisation through digital and encrypted apps
q.x: These protests were leaderless, coordinated online through encrypted apps, with no formal central committee.

q.s: Rehabilitation of people in deviant or vulnerable situations, such as drug addiction, beggary and juvenile delinquency, is termed:
q.x: This is social defence. Social welfare means targeted services for vulnerable groups.

q.s: The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, the rural employment law, is administered by the Ministry of:
q.x: It is run by the Ministry of Rural Development; Andhra Pradesh ranked first in the first 45 days.

q.s: Under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, the Centre-State funding ratio for most States is:
q.x: Funding is 60:40, and 90:10 for the North-Eastern and Himalayan States; the wage floor is Rs 300 a day.

q.s: India's social protection coverage, which was 22% in 2016, rose by 2025 to about:
q.x: Coverage rose to 64.3% in 2025, as per ILO data.

q.s: The Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK), which provides free delivery care in public facilities, was launched in:
q.x: JSSK began in 2011. Janani Suraksha Yojana began in 2005 and Mission Indradhanush in 2014.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT merged into the Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 scheme (2021)?
q.x: PM POSHAN, the school meal scheme, stays separate. The other three were merged.

q.s: The annual premium of the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), giving accident cover of Rs 2 lakh, is:
q.x: PMSBY costs Rs 20 a year; PMJJBY, a life cover for death from any cause, costs Rs 436.

q.s: Which of the following statements about social security schemes is correct?
o: PMJJBY gives life cover for accidental death only.
The annual premium of PMSBY is Rs 436.
PMJJBY, PMSBY and Atal Pension Yojana were launched on 9 May 2015.
Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana covered urban street vendors.
q.x: All three were launched on 9 May 2015. PMJJBY covers death from any cause (Rs 436), PMSBY costs Rs 20, and AABY covered rural landless households.

q.s: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) was launched in:
q.x: PM-JAY was launched in 2018. APY came in 2015 and e-Shram in 2021.

q.s: Which of the following schemes was NOT launched in 2015?
q.x: PM-JAY came in 2018; APY, PMJJBY and PMSBY were launched on 9 May 2015.

q.s: Under Stand-Up India, bank loans of Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore are given to:
q.x: Each bank branch must fund at least one SC/ST and one woman borrower.

q.s: The Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP, 2008) was formed by merging:
q.x: PMEGP merged the Rural Employment Generation Programme and the Prime Minister's Rozgar Yojana.

q.s: 'Sugamya Pustakalaya', launched for persons with print disabilities, is:
o: An online library of accessible books
q.x: It is an online library of books in DAISY, audio and Braille formats. PRASHAST is a disability-screening app.

q.s: China claims about 90,000 sq km of Indian territory in the north-east, most of it in:
q.x: China calls Arunachal 'South Tibet'; the USA has reaffirmed Arunachal as part of India.

q.s: India needed a waiver under the US law CAATSA (2017) mainly because of its purchase of the:
q.x: CAATSA targets buyers of Russian arms; India bought the Russian S-400.

q.s: The permanent Secretariat of BIMSTEC is located at:
q.x: The BIMSTEC Secretariat is at Dhaka; Kathmandu hosts the SAARC Secretariat.

q.s: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of BIMSTEC?
q.x: BIMSTEC has Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand; Maldives is not a member.

q.s: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas is observed on 9 January because on that day in 1915:
o: Gandhi returned to India from South Africa
The Indian National Congress held a session abroad
q.x: 9 January marks Gandhi's return from South Africa; the day was announced by Vajpayee in 2002.

q.s: Since 2015, the Pravasi Bharatiya Divas convention has been held:
q.x: Since 2015 the convention is biennial, with smaller events in between.

q.s: The 9th Conclave of Chiefs of the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium (IONS) was hosted in 2026 at:
q.x: Visakhapatnam, home of the Eastern Naval Command, hosted it; IONS has 25 members and 9 observers.

q.s: The trilateral India-Iran-Afghanistan agreement on Chabahar port was signed in:
q.x: It was signed in May 2016 during PM Modi's visit to Tehran; 2015 was the year of the MoU.

q.s: After the partition of India, the strength of the Constituent Assembly was reduced from 389 to:
q.x: After the Muslim League members from Pakistan areas left, the Assembly's strength fell to 299.

q.s: Of the 389 seats originally planned for the Constituent Assembly, the princely States were allotted:
q.x: 296 seats were for British India (292 provinces + 4 Chief Commissioner's provinces) and 93 for the princely States, at about one seat per 10 lakh population.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
q.x: J. B. Kripalani was not on the seven-member Drafting Committee chaired by Ambedkar.

q.s: D. P. Khaitan, a member of the Drafting Committee who died in 1948, was replaced by:
q.x: T. T. Krishnamachari replaced Khaitan; N. Madhava Rau replaced B. L. Mitter.

q.s: The 2022 ruling that wearing the hijab is not an essential religious practice of Islam was delivered by the High Court of:
q.x: The Karnataka High Court gave the ruling; a nine-judge bench under CJI Surya Kant is reviewing the essential-practices doctrine in 2026.

q.s: Under Article 22(7) of the Constitution, the maximum period of preventive detention may be prescribed by:
q.x: Clause (7) empowers Parliament to prescribe the maximum period; Advisory Boards consist of persons qualified to be High Court judges.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Article 22 is correct?
o: The President prescribes the maximum period of preventive detention.
Grounds of detention need never be communicated to the detenu.
Advisory Boards consist of Members of Parliament.
Only Parliament can make preventive detention laws on defence, foreign affairs and the security of India.
q.x: Such laws are on the Union List. Parliament fixes the maximum period, Advisory Boards have persons qualified to be High Court judges, and grounds must be communicated.

q.s: The Fundamental Right to education (Article 21A) for children of 6 to 14 years was inserted by the:
q.x: The 86th Amendment (2002) inserted Article 21A, following Mohini Jain (1992) and Unnikrishnan (1993); the RTE Act followed in 2009.

q.s: Under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, the share of entry-level seats in unaided private schools reserved for weaker sections is:
q.x: The 25% quota applies to unaided private schools but not to minority schools.

q.s: Article 15(5), enabling reservation in admission to private unaided educational institutions, was inserted by the:
q.x: The 93rd Amendment (2005) undid the effect of P. A. Inamdar (2005), which had barred such quotas.

q.s: The right to work, to education and to public assistance in certain cases is a Directive Principle under Article:
q.x: Article 41 covers the right to work. Article 43 is about a living wage; whether the right to work should be a Fundamental Right was debated in the Constituent Assembly.

q.s: The 24th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1971 was enacted in response to the Supreme Court's judgment in:
q.x: Golaknath (1967) had held that Parliament could not amend Fundamental Rights; the 24th Amendment amended Articles 13 and 368.

q.s: The amendment that made it obligatory for the President to give assent to a Constitution Amendment Bill was the:
q.x: The 24th Amendment (1971) made Presidential assent mandatory. The 25th inserted Article 31C.

q.s: After the 44th Amendment, a proclamation of National Emergency can be issued by the President only on the:
o: Oral advice of the Prime Minister
Written recommendation of the Union Cabinet
Advice of the Chief Justice of India
q.x: The 44th Amendment (1978) requires the Cabinet's written recommendation, so the PM's oral advice alone is not enough.

q.s: All doubts and disputes arising out of the election of the Vice-President of India are decided by the:
q.x: Under Article 71 the Supreme Court decides such disputes; the 39th Amendment had removed this power and the 44th restored it.

q.s: The oath of office to the Vice-President of India is administered by the:
q.x: Under Article 69 the President administers the oath to the Vice-President; the CJI administers it to the President.

q.s: To whom among the following is the oath of office NOT administered by the President?
q.x: A Governor takes oath before the Chief Justice of the High Court (Art. 159).

q.s: The Chief Election Commissioner of India is appointed by the:
q.x: The President appoints the CEC; this is not an electoral function of Parliament.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an electoral function of Parliament?
o: Taking part in the election of the President
Electing the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
q.x: The CEC is appointed by the President. The other three are electoral functions of Parliament or its Houses.

q.s: Notice of the resolution to impeach the President under Article 61 must be signed by at least:
o: One-tenth of the members of the House
One-fourth of the members of the House
One-half of the members of the House
Two-thirds of the members of the House
q.x: The charge needs a notice signed by one-fourth of the House and 14 days' notice; passing it needs two-thirds of the total membership.

q.s: A privilege motion moved in either House of Parliament is referred to the:
q.x: It goes to the Committee of Privileges; it censures a Minister and does not force the Government out.

q.s: Which of the following statements about a privilege motion is correct?
o: It can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
It is referred to the Ethics Committee.
If adopted, it forces the Government to resign.
It is moved when a Minister withholds or distorts the facts of a case.
q.x: It can be moved in either House, goes to the Committee of Privileges and only censures the Minister.

q.s: Once a resolution has been moved in Parliament, a resolution on substantially the same subject cannot be moved within:
q.x: The bar is one year; a resolution is a substantive motion withdrawn only by leave of the House.

q.s: The adjournment motion, used to draw attention to a definite matter of urgent public importance, can be moved only in the:
q.x: Only the Lok Sabha has the adjournment motion; it needs 50 members' support and a debate of at least 2 hours 30 minutes.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the passing of the Budget in Parliament is correct?
o: The Rajya Sabha votes on the Demands for Grants.
The Lok Sabha may increase a Demand for Grant.
The Appropriation Bill is passed before the Finance Bill.
A vote of credit is a normal stage of every Budget.
q.x: The Appropriation Bill precedes the Finance Bill. Demands are voted only in the Lok Sabha, which may only pass, reject or reduce them.

q.s: Of the 175 seats in the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly, the number reserved for Scheduled Castes is:
q.x: 29 seats are for SCs and 7 for STs; AP also has 25 Lok Sabha seats.

q.s: The nomination of Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies was ended by the:
q.x: The 104th Amendment ended Anglo-Indian nomination from 25 January 2020.

q.s: Which of the following statements comparing the Indian and British systems is correct?
o: India's Head of State is directly elected.
British courts can strike down Acts of Parliament.
India's Head of State is hereditary.
q.x: Britain has an unwritten Constitution and a sovereign Parliament whose Acts courts cannot strike down; India's President is indirectly elected for five years.

q.s: The first regular Chief Justice of the Andhra Pradesh High Court at Amaravati, sworn in on 7 October 2019, was:
q.x: J. K. Maheshwari was the first regular CJ; C. Praveen Kumar was acting CJ from 1 January 2019.

q.s: 'Epistolary jurisdiction' of the higher judiciary refers to:
o: Hearing only formal writ petitions filed by advocates
Treating letters, postcards and news reports as petitions
Issuing advisory opinions to the President
q.x: Under epistolary jurisdiction, part of judicial activism since the late 1970s, letters can be treated as PILs.

q.s: The Supreme Court struck down the clauses excluding High Court review of tribunal decisions under Articles 323-A and 323-B in:
q.x: L. Chandra Kumar (1997) held judicial review to be basic structure; tribunal decisions lie before a High Court bench.

q.s: Dr B. R. Ambedkar described the Indian federation as:
o: An indestructible Union of indestructible States
A destructible Union of indestructible States
An indestructible Union of destructible States
q.x: The Union is not the result of an agreement among States, and States have no right to secede; their boundaries can be altered.

q.s: Parliament can alter the area or boundaries of a State under Article 3 by:
o: A special majority with State consent
A simple majority, without the State's consent
A two-thirds majority and ratification by half the States
q.x: Only a simple majority is needed; the President refers the Bill to the State legislature for its views, which are not binding.

q.s: The Inter-State Council is established by the President by order under Article:
q.x: Article 263 provides for it; the PM chairs the Council and the Union Home Minister its Standing Committee.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Inter-State Council?
q.x: The Council has the PM, the CMs of States and UTs with legislatures, Administrators of other UTs and six Cabinet Ministers; the CJI is not a member.

q.s: The 14th Finance Commission raised the States' share in the divisible pool of central taxes to:
q.x: The 14th raised it from 32% to 42%, the largest increase; the 15th set it at 41%.

q.s: The number of members of a State Public Service Commission is determined by the:
q.x: The Governor fixes a State PSC's strength; the President fixes the UPSC's. During an inquiry a State PSC member is suspended by the Governor but removed by the President.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Public Service Commissions is correct?
o: At least half the members must have held government office for ten years.
During an inquiry, a State PSC member is suspended by the President.
The strength of a State PSC is fixed by the President.
The UPSC must have exactly 20 members.
q.x: Half the members must have ten years of government service. The Governor fixes a State PSC's strength and suspends its members; the UPSC usually has 9-11 members.

q.s: In India, a death sentence can be pardoned only by the:
q.x: Only the President can pardon a death sentence under Article 72; the Governor's power under Article 161 does not extend to it.

q.s: Murder (old IPC Section 302) is now punishable under Section 103 of the:
q.x: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita is the penal code; the BNSS is the procedure code.

q.s: The Central Vigilance Commission, set up in 1964 by an executive resolution, was given statutory status by the:
q.x: The CVC Act, 2003 made the Commission a statutory body.

q.s: The Central Vigilance Commission exercises superintendence in corruption cases over the:
q.x: The CVC supervises the CBI in corruption cases; its members have fixed terms, not office at the President's pleasure.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Central Vigilance Commission is correct?
o: Its members hold office at the pleasure of the President.
It is an independent statutory body under the CVC Act, 2003.
It was set up in 2003 by an executive resolution.
q.x: It became statutory in 2003; it was set up in 1964 by resolution. Members have a fixed term of 4 years or till 65.

q.s: In the Corruption Perceptions Index 2025, released on 10 February 2026, India's rank was:
q.x: India ranked 91st of 182 with a score of 39, up from 96th (score 38) in CPI 2024.

q.s: Under Centrally Sponsored Schemes, the core schemes are funded by the Centre and the States in the ratio:
q.x: Core schemes are 60:40; the Centre setting the parameters is why CSS are said to squeeze State priorities.

q.s: The committee of Chief Ministers on digital payments set up in 2016 was convened by:
q.x: Chandrababu Naidu convened the digital payments committee (and the 2015 Swachh Bharat sub-group); Chouhan convened the CSS rationalisation sub-group.

q.s: The Prime Ministers of the United Front governments of 1996-98 were:
o: H. D. Deve Gowda and I. K. Gujral
H. D. Deve Gowda and Chandra Shekhar
V. P. Singh and Chandra Shekhar
A. B. Vajpayee and I. K. Gujral
q.x: Deve Gowda and Gujral led the United Front; the Congress withdrew outside support from Deve Gowda in 1997.

q.s: Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, an election petition is tried by the:
q.x: Section 80A gives the High Court jurisdiction; the petition must be filed within 45 days of the result (Section 81).

q.s: The principle that a function should be performed at the lowest competent level of government, invoked by the Second ARC, is known as:
q.x: Subsidiarity places each function at the lowest level able to perform it.

q.s: Which of the following statements on centralisation and decentralisation in India is correct?
o: Nation-building after Partition was an argument for centralisation.
Subsidiarity means performing a function at the highest level of government.
Elite capture by dominant castes was an argument for decentralisation.
The Second ARC opposed the principle of subsidiarity.
q.x: The need for unity after Partition favoured centralisation; fear of elite capture also favoured it. The Second ARC invoked subsidiarity.

q.s: Under Part IX of the Constitution, the minimum share of seats in Panchayats reserved for women is:
q.x: Article 243D reserves at least one-third of seats for women; SC/ST seats are by population and rotation.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an item of the Twelfth Schedule (functions of municipalities)?
o: Vital statistics including registration of births and deaths
q.x: Libraries, like technical training and vocational education, is an Eleventh Schedule (Panchayat) item.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Domestic Systemically Important Insurer (D-SII) for FY 2025-26?
q.x: The D-SIIs are LIC, GIC Re and New India Assurance; HDFC Bank is a D-SIB (bank).

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh's IT & GCC Policy 4.0, the scheme 'LIFT' stands for:
q.x: LIFT is the Land Incentive for Tech Hubs; the IT & GCC Policy 4.0 was issued on 12 December 2024.

q.s: The Polavaram irrigation project on the Godavari was declared a national project under which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
q.x: Section 90 declares Polavaram a national project, so the Centre funds its completion.

q.s: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission's 12th Report, which suggested the Sevottam model, dealt with:
q.x: The 12th Report, 'Citizen Centric Administration', also recommended statutory backing for Citizens' Charters.

q.s: The oldest agrarian pressure group in India, founded in 1936, is the:
q.x: The All India Kisan Sabha was founded in 1936; Raju Shetti's Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana is based in Maharashtra.

q.s: The Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards set up under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 function under the administrative control of the:
q.x: Both Boards are autonomous bodies under the Union (Ministry of Jal Shakti), which notified their jurisdiction on 15 July 2021.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the headquarters of the Krishna River Management Board is to be located in:
q.x: The Krishna Board sits in Andhra Pradesh and the Godavari Board in Telangana.

q.s: The rain-shadow, drought-prone region of Andhra Pradesh is:
q.x: Rayalaseema lies in the rain shadow and is drought-prone.

q.s: Which of the following rivers does NOT form a delta in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: The Tungabhadra is a tributary of the Krishna and has no delta; AP has the Godavari, Krishna and Penna deltas.

q.s: After the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, the equity of the Singareni Collieries Company Limited is held by Telangana and the Government of India in the ratio:
q.x: Telangana holds 51% and the Centre 49%; existing SCCL coal linkages of AP's thermal plants were kept unchanged.

q.s: Royalty on onshore oil and natural gas produced in a State accrues to:
q.x: Onshore royalty goes to the producing State; offshore royalty goes to the Union.

q.s: The fall in India's dependency ratio, from 79% in 1975 to about 48% by 2021, is mainly associated with a decline in:
q.x: Falling fertility reduces the share of children, lowering the dependency ratio.

q.s: The Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP) was extended to the whole country in:
q.x: IRDP went nationwide in 1980; DWCRA came in 1982, EAS in 1993 and SGRY in 2001.

q.s: Which of the following rural programmes was NOT launched in the 1980s?
q.x: SGRY came in 2001. IRDP (1980), DWCRA (1982) and JRY (1989) belong to the 1980s.

q.s: Saubhagya (Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana, 2017) is implemented by the Ministry of:
q.x: Saubhagya is a Ministry of Power scheme; RGGVY (2005) was subsumed in DDUGJY in 2015.

q.s: The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) was launched in the year:
q.x: PMGSY began on 25 December 2000; PMGSY-II came in 2013 and PMGSY-III in 2019.

q.s: Under PMGSY, habitations in LWE-affected blocks are eligible for road connectivity if their population is at least:
q.x: LWE blocks: 100+; hill, NE, desert and tribal areas: 250+; plains: 500+.

q.s: Visakhapatnam was selected under the Smart Cities Mission in:
q.x: Visakhapatnam was among the first 20 cities in January 2016; Amaravati came in Round 3.

q.s: The factor income earned abroad by a normal resident of India is included in India's:
q.x: GNP is based on normal residents and GDP on domestic territory, so income earned abroad counts only in GNP.

q.s: The new Consumer Price Index series released in 2026 has as its base year:
q.x: The new CPI has base 2024, replacing 2012; CPI is released by the NSO (MoSPI), not the RBI.

q.s: The revised Index of Industrial Production (IIP) has as its base year:
q.x: The IIP base was moved to 2022-23.

q.s: An economy moving from agriculture directly to services without passing through a manufacturing-led stage is described as the problem of the:
q.x: The 'missing middle' refers to the skipped manufacturing stage in India's structural change.

q.s: In W. Arthur Lewis's dual-sector model (1954), the 'turning point' is reached when:
o: Surplus farm labour drawn into modern industry is exhausted
Industrial wages fall below farm wages
q.x: Once the surplus farm labour runs out, wages in the modern sector begin to rise.

q.s: In India, the poverty line is measured on the basis of:
q.x: Poverty is measured by MPCE; a person whose consumption falls below the line is poor.

q.s: Under the N. C. Saxena Committee approach to identifying rural BPL households, which of the following are automatically included?
q.x: PVTGs, Maha Dalits, destitutes and bonded labourers are automatically included; tax payers and vehicle owners are excluded.

q.s: A UN expert team described which of the following as 'the principal shortcomings' of Indian planning?
q.x: Implementation failure is regarded as the chief drawback of Indian planning.

q.s: The expression 'Licence-Permit-Quota Raj' was coined by:
q.x: C. Rajagopalachari, founder of the Swatantra Party, coined it.

q.s: The Prime Minister called the 'father of Indian economic reforms', who took office on 21 June 1991, was:
q.x: P. V. Narasimha Rao led the 1991 reforms with Manmohan Singh as Finance Minister.

q.s: GST 2.0 (2025) introduced a special slab for sin and luxury goods at the rate of:
q.x: GST 2.0 moved to two main slabs (5% and 18%) with a special 40% slab.

q.s: Which of the following taxes was NOT subsumed in the Goods and Services Tax?
q.x: Stamp duty remains outside GST. GST is destination-based, and input tax credit ends cascading.

q.s: Statutory grants-in-aid to States under Article 275 are given on the recommendation of the:
q.x: Article 275 grants are recommended by the Finance Commission and charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

q.s: Discretionary grants for any public purpose are made under Article:
q.x: Article 282 grants are discretionary and voted, not charged.

q.s: The 11th meeting of the Governing Council of NITI Aayog (11 June 2026), attended by all 28 Chief Ministers, had the theme:
o: Inclusive Human Development for Viksit Bharat@2047
q.x: The 11th meeting's theme was Inclusive Human Development; the 10th (2025) was Viksit Rajya for Viksit Bharat@2047.

q.s: Zero Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) has applied to RuPay debit card and BHIM-UPI transactions since:
q.x: Zero MDR began on 1 January 2020; NPCI is the nodal agency for the RuPay-BHIM UPI incentive scheme.

q.s: Gains from the transfer of cryptocurrencies (virtual digital assets) in India are taxed at:
q.x: The Finance Act, 2022 taxes such gains at 30% with 1% TDS; it did not make crypto legal tender.

q.s: The RBI's 2018 circular barring banks from dealing with crypto businesses was struck down in 2020 by the:
q.x: The Supreme Court struck it down in the IAMAI case (2020).

q.s: At the launch of the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana in 2015, the maximum loan was:
q.x: The cap was Rs 10 lakh (Shishu, Kishore, Tarun).

q.s: The 'Tarun Plus' category under MUDRA, for Tarun borrowers who have repaid earlier loans, covers loans of:
q.x: Tarun Plus covers Rs 10-20 lakh.

q.s: The Central Office of the Reserve Bank of India, first set up at Calcutta, was moved to Bombay in:
q.x: The RBI began at Calcutta in 1935 and its Central Office moved to Bombay in 1937.

q.s: The Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance (1926), which recommended a central bank for India, is also known as the:
q.x: The Hilton Young Commission's report led to the RBI Act, 1934; Ambedkar gave evidence before it.

q.s: The Monetary Policy Committee of the Reserve Bank of India has how many members?
q.x: The MPC has six members, three from the RBI and three appointed by the Government.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Reserve Bank of India?
q.x: Fiscal policy is made by the Ministry of Finance. Credit is created by commercial banks; the RBI controls it.

q.s: The first demonetisation after Independence, of Rs 1,000, Rs 5,000 and Rs 10,000 notes, took place on:
q.x: The 1978 demonetisation was the first after Independence; 1946 was before it and 2016 covered Rs 500 and Rs 1,000 notes.

q.s: In May 2023 the RBI withdrew from circulation, while keeping it legal tender, the currency note of:
q.x: The Rs 2,000 note was withdrawn from circulation but remains legal tender.

q.s: The first private sector bank set up after the 1994 liberalisation of bank licensing was:
q.x: UTI Bank, now Axis Bank, was the first of the new private banks.

q.s: The first bank in India to be run entirely by Indians was the:
q.x: The Oudh Commercial Bank (1881) was the first bank run by Indians.

q.s: The gross NPA ratio of scheduled commercial banks fell in September 2025 to a multi-decadal low of about:
q.x: Gross NPAs fell to 2.2%, helped by the 4R strategy for public sector banks.

q.s: The 58.77 crore accounts recorded in August 2026 belong to the:
q.x: They are PMJDY accounts; 99.92% of villages have a banking outlet within 5 km.

q.s: The Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025 raised the 'substantial interest' threshold in a company from Rs 5 lakh to:
q.x: The Act, in force from 1 August 2025, raised it to Rs 2 crore and the tenure of co-operative bank directors from 8 to 10 years.

q.s: A bank asset that has remained a non-performing asset for 12 months or less is classified as:
q.x: Sub-standard: NPA up to 12 months; doubtful: over 12 months; loss: loss identified but not written off.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a category of non-performing assets?
q.x: SMA-2 (61-90 days overdue) is still a standard asset; NPAs are sub-standard, doubtful or loss assets.

q.s: Under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, the NCLT is to admit or reject an application for the corporate insolvency resolution process within:
q.x: The admission decision is to be made within 14 days.

q.s: The pre-packaged insolvency resolution process for MSMEs under the IBC is to be completed within:
q.x: The pre-pack process for MSMEs has a 120-day limit.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a parameter tracked under the RBI's Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) framework for banks?
q.x: PCA watches capital, asset quality (NPAs) and leverage; the credit-deposit ratio is not a PCA parameter.

q.s: Which of the following would help ease the effect of supply shocks on food inflation?
q.x: Efficient storage and distribution soften supply shocks; hoarding, MSP hikes and expectations add to inflation.

q.s: Under GST, an e-way bill for the movement of goods is generally valid for one day for every:
q.x: Validity is one day per 200 km; e-way bills apply to both inter-State and intra-State movement above Rs 50,000.

q.s: In the now fully government-owned Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN), the Centre and the States hold shares in the ratio:
q.x: The Centre and the States together hold 50% each.

q.s: The Health Security se National Security Cess on pan masala units is levied on the basis of:
q.x: It is assessed on machine capacity; being a cess, its revenue is not shared with the States.

q.s: The Interim Budget 2024-25 proposed coal gasification and liquefaction capacity, to be achieved by 2030, of:
q.x: The target was 100 MT by 2030.

q.s: In the Interim Budget 2024-25, viability gap funding for an initial capacity of 1 GW was proposed for:
q.x: The VGF was for offshore wind; CBG blending in CNG and PNG was to be phased in as mandatory.

q.s: The largest component of India's foreign exchange reserves is:
q.x: FCA is the largest component; the RTP, an unconditional drawing right on the IMF quota, is the smallest.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of India's foreign exchange reserves?
q.x: Reserves are FCA, gold, SDRs and RTP; NRI deposits and World Bank loans are not.

q.s: Which of the following pulses is a kharif crop?
q.x: Tur is a kharif pulse; gram, lentil and peas are rabi pulses.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a rabi crop?
q.x: Jute is a kharif crop.

q.s: The National Rainfed Area Authority (NRAA) was set up in:
q.x: The NRAA was set up in 2006; rainfed farming covers about 50-60% of the net sown area.

q.s: Which of the following statements about rainfed and sustainable agriculture is correct?
o: Sustainable agriculture puts present needs first, even at a cost to the land.
Rainfed farming covers about 50-60% of the net sown area.
The National Rainfed Area Authority was set up in 2010.
q.x: Rainfed farming covers about half or more of the net sown area. Sustainable agriculture protects land for future generations, its pillars include equity, and the NRAA dates from 2006.

q.s: A major trigger of farmer suicides in India, as identified in studies of agrarian distress, is:
q.x: Usurious informal loans lead to distress sale of land or gold and bonded-labour-like ties.

q.s: The slogan 'One Nation, One Crop, One Premium' is associated with the:
q.x: PMFBY (2016) carries the slogan; AP's Dr YSR Free Crop Insurance (2019-24) had the State pay the whole premium.

q.s: NABARD's SHG-Bank Linkage Programme, regarded as the world's largest microfinance programme, was launched in:
q.x: It began in 1992.

q.s: The Lead Bank Scheme was introduced in the same year as the nationalisation of 14 banks, namely:
q.x: Both came in 1969.

q.s: Free foodgrain under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) has been extended up to:
q.x: PMGKAY, covering over 80 crore NFSA beneficiaries, runs till 31 December 2028.

q.s: Fortified rice supplied through the PDS is fortified with:
o: Iodine, vitamin A and vitamin D
Iron, folic acid and vitamin B12
q.x: Fortified rice carries iron, folic acid and vitamin B12.

q.s: The Arjun Sengupta Committee (1984) on public enterprises recommended autonomy leading to the:
q.x: It led to the MoU system; the Rangarajan Committee (1993) dealt with disinvestment.

q.s: A Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE) is a company in which the Central Government or other CPSEs hold at least:
q.x: 51% or more; the Public Enterprises Survey excludes banks and insurers.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT covered by the Public Enterprises Survey?
q.x: The Survey, prepared by DPE on the advice of the Estimates Committee, leaves out banks, insurers and departmental undertakings.

q.s: Since July 2021, the Department of Public Enterprises has functioned under the Ministry of:
q.x: DPE moved to the Ministry of Finance in July 2021; it grants Ratna status itself.

q.s: Board-level executives of Central Public Sector Enterprises are selected by the:
q.x: The PESB selects board-level executives of CPSEs.

q.s: The largest agro-based industry in India is the:
q.x: Textiles is the largest agro-based industry, with sugar next.

q.s: The first industrial policy in India to give strong emphasis to exports was the:
q.x: The 1980 Statement stressed modernisation and export orientation.

q.s: The MRTP Act, 1969 was replaced by the:
q.x: The Competition Act, 2002 replaced the MRTP Act.

q.s: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948, which laid the basis of a mixed economy, was announced by the Industry Minister:
q.x: Syama Prasad Mookerjee, the first Industry Minister, announced it.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT placed under exclusive Central monopoly by the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948?
q.x: Iron and steel was in the mixed category, where only the State would start new units; the other three were Central monopolies.

q.s: Under asset monetisation of brownfield public assets, the government:
o: Leases the assets for a fixed period without transferring ownership
Sells the assets outright to private firms
q.x: The assets are leased for a fixed period and ownership stays with the government.

q.s: The three-capitals plan of Andhra Pradesh (2020) was based mainly on the reports of the:
o: G. N. Rao Committee and the BCG study
q.x: The 2020 plan relied on the G. N. Rao Committee and the Boston Consulting Group study.

q.s: The expert committee set up under Section 6 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 to study options for a new capital was headed by:
q.x: The Sivaramakrishnan Committee (August 2014) opposed a single 'super capital'.

q.s: Under Special Category Status, Centrally Sponsored Schemes in a State are funded by the Centre and the State in the ratio:
q.x: SCS gives an automatic 90:10 grant; AP's Special Assistance Package gives the equivalent only through EAP repayments.

q.s: The Jalayagnam programme of the united Andhra Pradesh aimed to bring under irrigation about:
q.x: It aimed to irrigate 1 crore acres and stabilise 21 lakh acres, mainly on the Krishna, Godavari and Pennar.

q.s: Recognised start-ups can claim a tax holiday for 3 consecutive years out of 10 under Section:
q.x: Section 80-IAC gives the tax holiday; recognised start-ups may also self-certify under labour and environment laws.

q.s: The 'angel tax' on start-ups was abolished for all classes of investors in the:
q.x: The Union Budget 2024-25 abolished angel tax.

q.s: The Indian city with the largest number of unicorn start-ups is:
q.x: Bengaluru leads; India has the 3rd-largest start-up ecosystem with over 2.47 lakh DPIIT-recognised start-ups.

q.s: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 was enacted by Parliament under Article:
q.x: Article 253 lets Parliament legislate to implement international agreements, here the Stockholm Conference (1972).

q.s: The Forest (Conservation) Act was enacted in the year:
q.x: Forest (Conservation) Act 1980; Air Act 1981; Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972; Water Cess Act 1977.

q.s: Which of the following Acts was NOT enacted in the 1980s?
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
q.x: The Wildlife (Protection) Act dates from 1972. The Forest Act (1980), Air Act (1981) and EP Act (1986) are from the 1980s.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of sustainable development?
q.x: Sustainable development balances growth, inclusion and the environment and rejects growth at any cost.

q.s: The Sustainable Development Goals of Agenda 2030 succeeded the:
q.x: Agenda 2030 grew out of the MDGs and the Rio+20 conference and is universal in character.

q.s: The three health-related Millennium Development Goals were merged into which Sustainable Development Goal?
q.x: SDG 3 covers good health and well-being.

q.s: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet at the IAU General Assembly held in August 2006 at:
q.x: The Prague General Assembly decided it; Pluto has not cleared its orbit.

q.s: The discovery that triggered the reclassification of Pluto was that of:
q.x: Eris, found to be about Pluto's size, prompted the IAU to define a planet.

q.s: Recent studies identify the main cause of the shifting of the Earth's rotation axis as:
o: Redistribution of mass as polar ice melts
q.x: Melting polar ice moves water towards the Equator; this has also lengthened the day by about 1.33 ms per century.

q.s: Tropical cyclones rarely form within about 5 degrees of the Equator because:
o: Sea temperatures are too low there
The Coriolis force is zero at the Equator
q.x: Cyclones need Coriolis deflection to spin up, and it vanishes at the Equator.

q.s: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following States?
q.x: It passes through eight States: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

q.s: For every one degree of longitude, the difference in local time is:
q.x: The Earth turns 360 degrees in 24 hours, so 1 degree = 4 minutes; local time is ahead to the east.

q.s: Compared with a place at 35 degrees W, the local time of a place at 25 degrees E is:
q.x: The places are 60 degrees apart; the eastern place is ahead by 60 x 4 = 240 minutes.

q.s: In the seismic shadow zone, direct P-waves are not recorded between about:
q.x: Direct P-waves are missing between 105 and 145 degrees; S-waves are absent beyond about 105 degrees.

q.s: Which of the following statements about seismic waves is correct?
o: Direct P-waves are not recorded between about 105 and 145 degrees from the epicentre.
S-waves are recorded at every place on the Earth.
All earthquakes share one fixed shadow zone.
q.x: This is the P-wave shadow zone. S-waves are absent beyond about 105 degrees, each quake has its own shadow zone, and P-waves pass through liquids.

q.s: The large pothole drilled into the river bed at the foot of a waterfall is called a:
q.x: Falling water and boulders drill a plunge pool below the fall.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an erosional landform of a river?
q.x: A delta is a depositional landform at the river's mouth.

q.s: The Mississippi river forms which type of delta?
q.x: The Mississippi has a bird's-foot delta; the Nile and Ganga are arcuate, the Tiber cuspate.

q.s: The Narmada and the Tapi enter the Arabian Sea through:
q.x: These west-flowing rivers have drowned, estuarine mouths.

q.s: The widest single continental shelf in the world, about 1,500 km wide, is the:
q.x: The Siberian shelf in the Arctic Ocean is the widest.

q.s: The ocean with the largest share of continental shelf is the:
q.x: The Atlantic has the largest share; the shelf is narrow where mountains run parallel to the coast, as in much of the Pacific.

q.s: The north-south extent of the Indian mainland is about:
q.x: North-south 3,214 km; east-west 2,933 km.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India's size is correct?
o: India is larger in area than Australia.
India's east-west extent is greater than its north-south extent.
India has about 2.4% of the world's land area.
India is the fifth largest country in the world.
q.x: India has 2.4% of the world's area and is the seventh largest country, after Australia; its north-south extent (3,214 km) exceeds its east-west extent (2,933 km).

q.s: Since Jammu and Kashmir became a Union Territory on 31 October 2019, Andhra Pradesh's rank among the States by area is:
q.x: AP is 7th after Rajasthan, MP, Maharashtra, UP, Gujarat and Karnataka.

q.s: Which of the following rivers rising in the Aravallis ends in the Rann of Kutch?
q.x: The Luni drains into the Rann of Kutch; the Sahibi flows north towards the Yamuna.

q.s: Which of the following rivers does NOT rise in the Aravalli range?
q.x: The Narmada rises at Amarkantak in the Maikal hills.

q.s: The largest biotic province of Andhra Pradesh, with about 53% of its forests, is the:
q.x: The Deccan Plateau has about 53% of AP's forests; the forests extend north to the Simhachalam hills and west to the Balaghat range.

q.s: Planting coastal shelterbelts and mangroves before cyclones is an example of:
q.x: Coastal vegetation buffers wind and storm surge, so planting it is a mitigation measure.

q.s: Weak governance and poor coordination among agencies are examples of which type of vulnerability?
q.x: They are institutional vulnerability; mangrove loss is environmental vulnerability. Risk falls as coping capacity rises.

q.s: Which of the following statements about disaster vulnerability is correct?
o: Disaster risk rises as coping capacity increases.
Loss of mangroves that raises cyclone impact is environmental vulnerability.
Weak governance is a form of physical vulnerability.
q.x: Mangrove loss is environmental vulnerability. Insurance reduces vulnerability, risk falls as coping capacity rises, and weak governance is institutional vulnerability.

q.s: The Geological Survey of India was set up in the year:
q.x: The GSI was founded in 1851; the ASI dates from 1861.

q.s: Lonar Lake in Maharashtra is a:
q.x: Lonar was formed by a meteorite impact in the Deccan basalt.

q.s: In the production and consumption of coal, India ranks in the world:
o: Third, after China and the USA
q.x: India is the second largest producer and consumer of coal after China.

q.s: In terms of coal reserves, India ranks in the world:
q.x: India has the fifth largest coal reserves; coal meets about 55% of its primary energy needs.

q.s: The leading producer of jowar in India, accounting for more than half of the country's output, is:
q.x: Maharashtra leads in jowar; Rajasthan leads in bajra and Madhya Pradesh in pulses.

q.s: Which of the following crop and leading State pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Madhya Pradesh is the leading producer of pulses.

q.s: The Japanese automobile maker Isuzu has its manufacturing plant in Andhra Pradesh at:
q.x: Sri City hosts Isuzu and Kobelco; Kia's plant is at Anantapur.

q.s: The alumina refinery of NALCO is located at:
q.x: NALCO's refinery is at Damanjodi (Koraput) and its smelter at Angul.

q.s: Which of the following aluminium plant and location pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: NALCO's refinery is at Damanjodi (Koraput); Lohardaga supplies bauxite to HINDALCO.

q.s: The PM GatiShakti National Master Plan, a GIS-based platform for infrastructure planning, was launched on:
q.x: It was launched on 13 October 2021, bringing together 16 ministries.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three economic rail corridors under PM GatiShakti?
q.x: The three corridors are Energy-Mineral-Cement, Port Connectivity and High Traffic Density.

q.s: The Ramappa Temple in Telangana was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in:
q.x: Ramappa and Dholavira were inscribed in 2021; Santiniketan and the Hoysala temples in 2023.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT yet a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
q.x: Lepakshi is only on the tentative list. Ramappa and Dholavira (2021) and the Moidams (2024) are inscribed.

q.s: The hill village known as the 'Kashmir of Andhra Pradesh' is:
q.x: Lambasingi in the Eastern Ghats records very low winter temperatures.

q.s: Which of the following pairs relating to tourism in Andhra Pradesh is NOT correctly matched?
o: Araku Valley - Alluri Sitharama Raju district
q.x: Maredumilli is in Polavaram district, not Nandyal.
